summary: Coup is a fast, cutthroat bluffing game where players claim character powers they may or may not actually hold, daring others to challenge them. It's tense and social, with the whole game riding on reading opponents' nerve and managing your dwindling influence cards.
praised: great for groups who enjoy social deduction
high replayability despite tiny card count
criticised: player elimination can leave people waiting out a round
some feel it's more about table read than skill

interaction.detail: Every action can be challenged or blocked by any other player, and coup/assassinate actions directly strip opponents of influence cards, so the game is almost entirely about player-vs-player confrontation. There's no personal board; the shared state is just coins and each player's hidden two cards, constantly under threat.

scoring.why: There's no scoring; the last player left with any influence cards remaining wins outright.
scoring.how_you_win: You win by successfully bluffing, blocking, and eliminating opponents' influence cards until you're the last family standing.
